newsitem.title: UK: CELLNET TO TAKE CHARGE AFTER BILLING ROW.
newsitem.headline: CELLNET TO TAKE CHARGE AFTER BILLING ROW.

text.p: Cellnet, the British mobile telephone operator owned by British Telecommunications and Securicor, said on Wednesday it planned to take an additional 40 million stg charge in 1998 after a row over a new billing system.

Securicor, which owns 40 percent of Cellnet, said if the provision were made after problems with the so-called ForCe project, it would also provide an extra 16 milion stg in its accounts in the year to September 1997.

The row over the new billing system, which is supposed to meet anticipated demand in the next century, came to a head when the company designing the project said it planned to gradually withdraw from the deal.

Cellnet, Britain's second-biggest cellular operator, said telecoms billing systems provider AMS Management Systems UK was in material breach of its contract and has given the company 30 days to come back with a solution.

But Cellnet said despite the dispute, it had not depended entirely on the ForCe project and had made alternative plans to ensure that its existing billing system would still meet the demands of both the company and its customers for the foreseeable future.

"As a market leader, Cellnet is committed to continuously improving the service it offers and the company is therefore already reviewing the options for upgrading its systems to meet the needs of the 21st century, should AMS fail to provide an acceptable solution," it stated in a letter to Securicor.

Cellnet has already made a provision of 25 million stg against its accounts in the year to March 31, 1997. Securicor has so far made a provision of 10 million stg for the six months to March 31, 1997.
